steps.title: Decide OAuth vs Personal Access Token
steps.detail: If the integration is for your own account or a script, consider a Personal Access Token; for multi-user apps register an OAuth2 Application.

evidence.note: V2 docs describe both Personal Access Tokens and OAuth2 options.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Sign in to Harvest ID and open Developers page
steps.detail: Authenticate to id.getharvest.com and go to the Developers/Applications area to create a new OAuth2 app.

evidence.note: Docs point to the Harvest ID Developers page for app registration; a live check of the page requires sign-in.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Register the OAuth2 Application
steps.detail: Provide app name, redirect URI(s), select product support (Harvest/Forecast) and copy client_id and client_secret from the console into your secure store.

evidence.note: Authentication docs describe fields returned and required for client credentials and redirect URIs.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Implement Authorization Code flow (server-side)
steps.detail: Redirect users to the documented authorize URL, capture the authorization code, exchange it for tokens at the documented token endpoint, and persist tokens securely.

evidence.note: Docs provide authorize and token endpoints; live probes showed the authorize page redirects to sign-in and the token endpoint rejects malformed requests indicating the endpoint is live and expects client_secret.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Implement token refresh and secure storage
steps.detail: Use refresh_token grant to obtain new access tokens. Store refresh tokens and client_secret on the server side and rotate as needed.

evidence.note: OAuth token example in docs includes expires_in and refresh token usage.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Test authorization and basic API calls
steps.detail: Authorize your app as a user, confirm returned scopes, call GET https://id.getharvest.com/api/v2/accounts and a sample API endpoint such as GET https://api.harvestapp.com/v2/users/me with Authorization and Harvest-Account-Id headers.

evidence.note: Docs show accounts endpoint and example API requests including required headers and User-Agent policy.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: (Optional) Expose/point to MCP connector for assistant integrations
steps.detail: If integrating with AI assistants using Harvest's MCP connector, follow the MCP connector instructions and provide the MCP URL and connector config to the assistant platform.

evidence.note: MCP docs describe connector URLs and usage patterns for assistants.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Deploy to production and monitor
steps.detail: Deploy your server, secure client_secret and refresh tokens, monitor token expiry and API rate limit (429 responses and Retry-After header), and provide user support contact info.

evidence.note: Production deployment and monitoring guidance references secure storage and rate limit awareness as inferred best practices, but explicit Harvest-required production deployment steps are not clearly documented.
evidence.label: unverified

steps.title: Use documented endpoints if discovery is not present
steps.detail: Harvest does not publish OIDC discovery at standard well-known URLs (probe). Use the explicit authorize and token endpoints from the documentation and configure any libraries manually.

evidence.note: Live probe found no .well-known discovery documents; docs list explicit endpoints to use instead.
evidence.label: sourced

nuances.text: No OIDC discovery: libraries expecting standard discovery documents must be manually configured with the documented authorize and token endpoints, issuer, and JWKS URL if you need JWT validation.

evidence.note: Because discovery documents were not found at probed URLs, you must provide endpoints to libraries manually; docs list explicit endpoints but do not provide a discovery document.
evidence.label: inferred

nuances.text: Token expiry and refresh: OAuth examples show expires_in in responses; typical example value shown corresponds to long-lived tokens (example in docs), handle refresh_token usage accordingly.

evidence.note: Authentication examples in the docs include expires_in and refresh_token fields.
evidence.label: sourced

nuances.text: Rate limits: Harvest enforces an API throttle of 100 requests per 15 seconds for general API endpoints and 100 requests per 15 minutes for Reports API; exceeding the limit returns 429 and Retry-After.

evidence.note: Rate limiting values and 429 behavior are documented in the V2 overview.
evidence.label: sourced

nuances.text: User-Agent requirement: every API call must include a User-Agent header containing your app name and a contact link or email; missing it triggers a 400 Bad Request.

evidence.note: V2 docs state the User-Agent header policy and consequences for omission.
evidence.label: sourced

nuances.text: App registration may require Administrator privileges on the Harvest account (legacy v1 doc indicates admin required).

evidence.note: V1 docs explicitly state an Administrator must register an app; V2 docs imply account context but do not repeat that line.
evidence.label: sourced

verdict.summary: Harvest provides a documented OAuth2 Authorization Code flow and a developer area for registering OAuth apps, so a developer can build and test an integration quickly; Harvest does not publish OIDC discovery metadata at common well-known URLs, so clients must use the documented endpoints. The API docs do not document a mandatory public app review or publishing process.

evidence.note: API v2 docs include explicit Authorization and token endpoints and describe app registration, enabling a quick dev setup.
evidence.label: sourced

timeToProd.assumes: You register an OAuth app in Harvest ID, implement the Authorization Code flow using documented scopes and endpoints, and you do not require a separate Harvest-managed app publishing review.

evidence.note: API docs describe how to register apps and show endpoints; MCP docs and API docs do not describe a mandatory public app review workflow.
evidence.label: sourced

timeToProd.waitingOn: No documented review required; wait only if Harvest requests additional information or support manually.

blockers.fix: Manually configure authorize/token endpoints and other values in your OAuth/OIDC library using the documented endpoints in Harvest API docs; file a support request if you need discovery metadata.
blockers.cause: Harvest does not publish OIDC discovery metadata at the well-known endpoints probed.
blockers.symptom: No .well-known/openid-configuration or oauth-authorization-server metadata at common hostnames

evidence.note: Live probe checked multiple common hostnames for .well-known documents and found none; docs provide explicit endpoints to use instead.
evidence.label: sourced

blockers.fix: Ensure you send client_id and client_secret and a valid authorization code in the token exchange. Test token exchange against the documented token endpoint using server-to-server POST with required form fields.
blockers.cause: Token endpoint enforces client credentials and grant parameter validation.
blockers.symptom: Token exchange returns client_secret required or invalid_request for malformed requests

evidence.note: Live probe to the token endpoint returned an error indicating client_secret is required; docs describe the token exchange parameters.
evidence.label: sourced

blockers.fix: Include a User-Agent header in every API request formatted per the docs, e.g. 'MyApp (https://example.com/contact)'.
blockers.cause: Harvest requires a User-Agent header that includes app name and contact; omission causes 400 responses.
blockers.symptom: API requests return 400 when User-Agent header is missing or malformed

evidence.note: V2 docs state missing User-Agent results in 400 and provide acceptable examples.
evidence.label: sourced

scopeTiers.impact: Access is limited to the specific Harvest account(s) the user authorizes. You must present and store Harvest-Account-Id when calling API endpoints.

evidence.note: V2 docs describe account-specific scope strings and the accounts endpoint to enumerate accessible accounts.
evidence.label: sourced

scopeTiers.impact: Grants the app access to all of a user's Harvest accounts, which increases the data and action surface your integration needs to handle.

evidence.note: Docs list harvest:all and similar scope strings for broader access.
evidence.label: sourced

scopeTiers.impact: Allows AI assistants that support the Harvest MCP connector to act on behalf of authorized users within role limits.

evidence.note: Harvest MCP documentation describes connector usage and assistant capabilities.
evidence.label: sourced

evidence.note: V1 docs explicitly say Administrator access is required to register an application; V2 docs assume account context for API calls and app setup.
evidence.label: sourced

prerequisites.why: Apps are created from the Harvest ID Developers page to obtain client_id and client_secret and to configure redirect URIs.

evidence.note: V2 Authentication docs describe registering an OAuth2 Application in Harvest ID developers.
evidence.label: sourced

prerequisites.why: Registration requires at least app name and redirect URI; contact/privacy details are typically needed when you surface the app to end users or for support.
prerequisites.item: Redirect URI and app contact/privacy info ready

evidence.note: No explicit requirement for redirect URI or app contact/privacy fields is enumerated in the official docs; this is an assumption based on general OAuth app registration norms.
